prompt: Some people think that all advertising aimed at children under the age of twelve should be banned. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
essay:
Children now meet commercial messages in more places than any previous generation, and there are recurring calls to prohibit advertising directed at the under-twelves altogether. I agree with a ban, principally because young children cannot recognise persuasion for what it is, although enforcing one is far harder than the proposal usually admits.

The central argument is about capacity. Advertising is a form of persuasion, and persuasion assumes an audience able to see that someone is trying to change its mind. Children below roughly eight lack that recognition entirely, and even at eleven the understanding is fragile under the pressure of an appealing image. Selling to an audience that cannot tell it is being sold to is not competition but exploitation of a known limitation, and the same reasoning already justifies preventing children from buying alcohol or entering a contract.

A second argument concerns content. The products marketed most heavily to children skew towards confectionery, sugary cereals and fast food, and the cumulative effect on what children come to expect from a meal is well recognised. Restrictions on this category alone have been introduced in several countries.

The difficulty is definitional. A ban on advertising aimed at children is straightforward for a toy commercial in a cartoon break, but far less so for product placement inside a game, a family film sponsored by a brand, or an online personality whose audience happens to be nine. Legislation covering only broadcast advertising simply moves the money online, where oversight is weakest and enforcement slowest.

On balance I support the ban, while recognising that it has to be written in terms of the audience actually reached rather than the audience formally intended. The test of a good rule here is whether a company could comply with its letter while defeating its purpose.
title: Advertising aimed at young children
